headline: Celtic scored seven, but Europe still says this is level
summary: Celtic warmed up for Celta Vigo with a 7-1 win over Hearts on Sunday. Europe tells a different story: two defeats, 0 points, 33rd of 36. Going forward they are fine — 2.28 expected goals a game — but the defence is unsettled, with Cameron Carter-Vickers a doubt. Celta have lost both their Europa League games too and average 1.17 expected goals, yet across bookmakers they are the narrowest favourites at 36.5%. The market makes this level: the handicap gives neither side a head start. Over 2.5 goals is rated 52.3%.
read: Celtic answered a 1-4 humbling at Benfica with a 7-1 thrashing of Hearts, but their European defence has now conceded seven goals in two games, and they are missing or doubting key centre-backs. Celta Vigo arrive after a 2-1 win over Alaves in which they were out-created, and the market rates the two sides level, with just over two and a half goals expected.

facts.fact: Both sides have lost both league-phase games: Celtic are 33rd of 36 on zero points with a -5 goal difference, Celta Vigo 28th with -2.
facts.meaning: Thursday's loser is left with almost no room to reach the knockout places, which is why both clubs are calling it a must-win.

facts.fact: Celta Vigo are the narrowest possible favourites: 36.5% to Celtic's 35.8%, with the handicap set at level (+0).
facts.meaning: This is a coin-flip in the market's eyes — neither side is rated even a fraction of a goal better.

facts.fact: Celtic warmed up with a 7-1 home win over Hearts on Sunday, their fourth game in 12 days.
facts.meaning: The attack is scoring freely going into a match Celtic have to win.

facts.fact: Celtic have conceded seven goals in their two Europa League defeats, 1-3 at home to Ferencvaros and 1-4 at Benfica.
facts.meaning: The defence is why Celtic are not favourites at home against a side that has also lost twice.

facts.fact: Celtic's most-used defender Cameron Carter-Vickers (814 minutes, 7.46 rating) is listed as a doubt but was back in training on Wednesday, while Auston Trusty has been ruled out for a private matter.
facts.meaning: Celtic's centre-back pairing is unsettled for the game they most need a clean sheet in.

facts.fact: Celta Vigo are without midfielder M. Roman, out with a knee injury after 669 minutes, one goal and two assists this season.
facts.meaning: Celta lose a regular starter from midfield in a match where the middle of the pitch decides who gets the first point.

facts.fact: Celta beat Alaves 2-1 on Sunday but were out-created, 0.97 xG to 1.06.
facts.meaning: Their results are running slightly ahead of their performances, which is why the market makes them only marginal favourites away from home.

facts.fact: The market expects goals: over 2.5 is priced at 52.3%, with a fair total of 2.6 goals.
facts.meaning: More likely than not, this is a game with three goals or more.

sources.fact: Shaun Maloney confirmed Auston Trusty will miss the Europa League clash with Celta Vigo due to a private matter.
Shaun Maloney confirmed Oliver Sorensen is back in Scotland and available for the Celta Vigo game.
Celtic bounced back from a dreadful European defeat to Benfica with a 7-1 win over Hearts in the Scottish Premiership.
Martin O'Neill's Celtic are looking to kickstart their European campaign with a much-needed three points against Celta Vigo.
Cameron Carter-Vickers and Alistair Johnston were spotted in Celtic training ahead of the Celta Vigo match.
Jota's game time is restricted to domestic games as he is not in Celtic's Europa League squad, so he will not face Celta Vigo.
Celta Vigo forward Ferran Jutgla described Thursday's Europa League encounter against Celtic as a hugely important fixture, with both clubs desperate for their first points.
Neither Celtic nor Celta Vigo have secured a point from their opening two league phase matches, leaving little room for error in their bid for knockout football.
